transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. So, uh, I’m here because I feel like I’m just always running hot, you know? Like I can’t shut the motor off. Which is funny, because I actually love working on motors. I was helping my buddy rebuild the engine on his old Chevy truck last weekend, and man, getting that alternator bracket to line up was a total nightmare. We must have spent three hours just looking for the right size socket wrench because his garage is an absolute disaster zone. I keep telling him he needs to put up a pegboard system, but he never listens, he just leaves his tools wherever they fall. Anyway, uh... wait, where was I going with that? Oh, right. My motor. Being unable to shut it off. Yeah, so lately that whole always-being-on thing has been getting me in a lot of trouble at the firehouse, so... here I am.

You mentioned feeling like you can't shut your motor off lately—would you say this feeling is something you've dealt with your whole life, or does it come and go in distinct episodes that are different from how you usually feel?

Man, I don't really know. I've never really thought about it like... episodes, or whatever. I guess I'm not sure if it's been forever? Like, I've just always been me, you know? But speaking of episodes, we had this absolute crazy call last Tuesday. Total chaos. This guy tried to deep fry a frozen turkey on his wooden deck, and, uh, you know how that goes. The oil just explodes everywhere. We roll up, and the whole back porch is just fully engulfed. And the guy is standing there in his flip-flops with a garden hose, which is literally the absolute worst thing you can do for a grease fire. I had to physically pull him back. I mean, water and oil, they just don't mix. It's like when I tried to make this fancy vinaigrette from scratch for my wife for our anniversary last year... I shook that mason jar for like twenty minutes and it still separated. I ended up just running to the store and buying the bottled stuff. She didn't even notice, thank god. But, uh... wait. What did you ask me? Something about how I usually feel?
Looking back over the last few years, have there been any periods of several days or weeks where you felt unusually low, sad, or hopeless?

Low, sad, or hopeless? No, I don't think so. I mean, I get bummed out sometimes, sure, but not for days or weeks at a time. Like, I was pretty annoyed last month when my favorite pizza place closed down. We used to go there every Friday after shift, you know? They had this amazing buffalo chicken slice with the perfect amount of ranch drizzled on top. Not too much ranch, just right. People always drown things in ranch, and it ruins the crust. It gets all soggy. I hate soggy pizza. Actually, that reminds me, my basement flooded a bit last spring, and getting that carpet ripped up was a nightmare. The smell alone... ugh. We had to rent one of those giant industrial fans. The guy at the rental place was super helpful, though. Showed me exactly how to set it up. He used to be a volunteer firefighter, actually, so we got to talking about gear and how heavy the new turnout coats are. But, yeah, no, I wouldn't say I get super sad or hopeless. Just... normal stuff, I guess.
Looking back at your time in elementary or middle school, did your teachers or parents ever comment on you being unable to sit still, constantly moving, or having trouble focusing on your schoolwork?

Yeah, actually, my mom says I was exactly like this back in grade school, too. Always popping out of my seat, blurting out answers before the teacher even finished asking the question, losing my homework... I swear, I used to get so many notes sent home. Which is crazy, because I was bright enough to do the work, I just... couldn't keep it together. Speaking of notes, we have this new dispatcher at the station, and she leaves these sticky notes everywhere. Like, everywhere. On the coffee maker, on the steering wheel of the rig... it's kind of driving me nuts. The other day, she left a note on the fridge saying "Please label your tupperware," but she used this neon pink pen that was almost impossible to read. I mean, who uses pink pen on a yellow sticky note? It's terrible contrast. I actually took a graphic design class back when I was getting my associate's degree, and color theory was like, week one. We had this project where we had to design a logo for a fake coffee shop, and I spent way too much time trying to pick the perfect shade of brown. I think I called it "The Daily Grind" or something cheesy like that. I got a B on it, though. But anyway, yeah, school... I was definitely a handful back then. Always moving around.
